messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — elevated 5xx and latency in eu-west-1 for /v1/generate. Trigger: error-rate > 10% for 2m. Pager: @Alex (oncall)
Alex: seeing it, looking now. paging infra-sre and runtime.
Alex: scope — user-visible errors on hosted API, mostly text-gen. embeddings seem fine.
Priya: I can repro a burst of 503s from the edge LB -> runtime. error traces show kv-cache misses and OOM in some pods.
Jared: stack traces point to a memory spike in runtime v2.3.2 kernel selection path. rolling back to v2.3.1 pod image might help.
Marta: we should avoid full rollback unless necessary. can we do traffic shaping first? reduce concurrent tokens, throttle long requests.
Sam: agree. recommend partial brownout: disable streaming for free-tier then p99 tokens cap at 2048 for everyone. That avoids heavy KV pressure.
Lydia: mass customer impact? Support dashboard shows ~12% API calls failing and a handful of paying customers reporting timeouts. No large enterprise SLA alerts yet.
Alex: decision tree: 1) immediate mitigations (rate-limit, quota change, feature disable) 2) regional reroute of new sessions to us-east-1 3) if no improvement, provider reroute/drain eu-west host pools.
product-ops: prepare customer comms with current symptoms + ETA. Prioritize paid customers.
support-ops: patch status page with "degraded performance — text generation in eu-west-1" and a note "investigating".
Alex: executing immediate mitigations. Commanding edge to apply per-key token-per-minute throttle for free-tier.
Alex: running: ```/opt/infra/bin/edgectl set-rate-limit --region eu-west-1 --matcher 'tier:free' --rps 5 --burst 10```
incident-bot: runbook check: increase token throttling -> apply quota reduction -> consider provider swap.
Priya: applying streaming toggle to off for free-tier routes now. patch config: ```routes.textgen.streaming.enabled=false --env eu-west-1 --selector tier=free```
Jared: launching gradual token cap enforcement for all keys to 2048 tokens max per request: ```/api/v1/configs/limits/update {\"max_tokens\":2048}```. Pushing to 5% of traffic -> 25% -> 100%.
Marta: results at 2m after first step: 5xx rate down from 12% -> 6%, p95 latency down 30%. looks promising.
Lydia: customers: two mid-market customers reported increased tail latency; escalation team engaged. No billing impact yet.
Alex: next: prepare region-level fallback for new sessions. We'll start new-session routing to us-east-1 for non-enterprise traffic. Existing sessions stay pinned.
Sam: configuring smart-routing policy: ```routerctl traffic-shape --from eu-west-1 --to us-east-1 --pct 30 --selector 'account_tier!=enterprise'```
Alex: starting 30% cutover now. monitoring errors and KV cache hit ratio.
incident-bot: metric snapshot: err-rate eu-west-1 -> 6% pre-cutover, after 30% -> 4.2%. us-east latencies increased 8% but within SLO.
Jared: confirming runtime pods in eu-west show reduced memory churn after shaping; single suspected host still OOM'ing occasionally.
Marta: run a targeted drain of that host to isolate. Command: ```orchestrator drain --region eu-west-1 --host host-1123 --grace-period 30s```
Alex: starting drain for host-1123. will set provider failover if we see instability during drain.
Priya: while draining, we need to lower quota for suspicious API keys that are high QPS. Querying top 50 keys by p90 usage.
Sam: applied automated quota reductions for top 12 noisy keys: `quotactl reduce --pct 40 --keys-file /tmp/noisy_keys.txt`.
Lydia: support-ops updated affected customers in thread DM with current mitigation and estimated recovery.
product-ops: preparing scheduled follow-up note for paid customers: explain transient brownout and actions taken.
Alex: on-call handoff at 12:30UTC incoming. @Jared will take after that; leaving summary.
Alex: SUMMARY - root cause investigation ongoing (runtime memory regression in v2.3.2). mitigations applied: 1) streaming disabled for free-tier 2) global token cap 2048 enforced progressively 3) per-key throttle for free accounts 4) 30% new-session reroute to us-east-1 5) host-1123 drained. Metrics improving but still watching.
Jared: taking second-half oncall. I'll monitor for escalation and be ready to flip provider reroute if drain causes fallthrough.
incident-bot: reminder: create follow-up ticket with postmortem template and assign to runtime team.
Marta: note — do not rollback v2.3.2 yet, we need full postmortem data. but create safe rollback playbook in case.
Priya: adding temporary kernel selection patch to runtime config to reduce mem overhead (non-disruptive). rolling to 10% now.
Sam: metrics at +20m: eu-west error rate down to 2.1%, overall p99 latency back near baseline. us-east stable. service-level impact largely mitigated.
Lydia: support — opening priority ticket for impacted paying accounts and offering credits where appropriate.
product-ops: draft customer-facing note: "We experienced degraded text-generation in eu-west-1. We applied traffic shaping and partial reroute; service is recovering. We'll follow up with root cause and remediation." will share in #announcements for review.
Alex: excellent. plan for next 2 hours: monitor, keep routing at 30% until runtime patch is at 50% rollout and stable. if error rate creeps >4% we escalate to provider reroute and capacity increase.
Jared: if we need provider-level reroute, runbook: `providerctl swap --from eu-west-provider-A --to eu-west-provider-B --grace 60s --dry-run` then cut 50% -> 100% if good. documented in ops playbooks.
incident-bot: escalations/owner changes logged. oncall handed to Jared at 12:30UTC.
Sam: quick retrospective note: consider prebuilt per-tenant token caps and more aggressive KV cache warming to avoid future mem pressure.
Marta: follow-up action items: create task for build-team to add conservative default for streaming memory usage; add synthetic load test to catch v2.x regressions.
Lydia: closing customer comms loop: support-ops will reach out to impacted customers by EOD local.
Alex: closing thread for live mitigation — will reopen if new incidents. great work everyone. :tada:
